conclusion: Native 3D lidar data is available and suitable for developing an external stair-entry localization layer; current code is not a validated two-step stair detector or motor-control gate.

scene_user_report.distance_reference: front feet to bottom riser base

hardware_model: Unitree native utlidar; exact L1/L2 product not independently identified from read-only metadata

live_sample.clock_note: Timestamp compatibility observed; independent clock calibration not established

additional_capture.visual_observation: Two riser-like vertical transitions visible in forward x-z profile; upper tread sparse, not a validated detector result.

code_findings.finding: min_steps=3 and explicit rejection of configurations below 3; incompatible with recognizing exactly two risers by design.
Requires broad three-lane coverage over forward ROI and rejects mixed vertical bins; this scan is sparse/occluded and includes a rear wall.
step_candidates_enabled=false; 2.5D infrastructure exists, full stair geometry not enabled or validated.
Navigation accumulator clips native-world z to [0.2,0.8] metres; use deskewed/native full clouds instead of this height-cropped navigation product.
Existing code rejects out-of-range elevations; current HeightMap includes NaN and 1e9 values, which cannot be treated as real surfaces.

integration.preserve_model_possible: External perception -> command supervisor -> existing MoE action decoder and guards
integration.required_controller_work: Current MoE adapter permits vx only 0 or 0.6 and hardcodes lateral/yaw commands to zero; variable approach speed and heading require interface changes.
integration.anticipatory_foot_placement: Needs a terrain-conditioned policy and training, or another compatible control method; an outer speed layer alone does not add terrain observations to MoE.

remaining: Two-riser specific geometry and multi-frame confirmation
Independent distance/height/heading ground truth, negative scenes and dynamic latency validation
Explicit wall/platform separation and visible-footprint/occlusion handling
The previous 0.9 rad tracking guard failures are not resolved by adding lidar
